f_01M12F6MBBMHZAS8E7XAQF57V0.subject: addition_phase_flow
f_01M12F6MBBMHZAS8E7XAQF57V0.content: Every TCR addition runs four blocks in fixed order: Retro (pre-addition work on the existing home), Exterior (demo → foundation → framing/shell → exterior finishes), Interior (rough MEPs → rough inspections → insulation/drywall → interior finishes), then Closeout.

f_01M12F6MBCZBC7N34F44NFYFGT.subject: addition_retrofit_signals
f_01M12F6MBCZBC7N34F44NFYFGT.content: Retrofit work embedded in an addition scope is detected via three signals: area mismatch (a room/feature outside the addition objective), the word "existing" appearing in scope text, or spatial ambiguity about a new feature's location relative to the addition footprint.

f_01M12F6MBCCHH9HRVF2B1HY883.subject: addition_pm_closeout_milestone
f_01M12F6MBCCHH9HRVF2B1HY883.content: The job-complete milestone on every addition is the PM's personal walkthrough with the customer, occurring one working day after the last item (final inspection, landscaping, exterior finishes, and deck) is finished.

f_01M12F6MBCNY9FN8MA0HPS0486.subject: addition_drywall_cracking_handling
f_01M12F6MBCNY9FN8MA0HPS0486.content: Hairline drywall cracks at new-to-existing tie-ins (above doors, windows, headers) are an expected year-one settling issue, covered by the 1-year labor warranty as a return visit rather than being scheduled as a job task.

f_01M12F6MBCT8Q1XRTSGYJHH0SJ.subject: addition_pacing_rule
f_01M12F6MBCT8Q1XRTSGYJHH0SJ.content: Everything on an addition before interior finishes is time-pressured; from interior finishes onward there is intentional schedule slack, and the back half should not be panic-compressed.

f_01M12F6MBCKAA7VVGRAHWGXB62.subject: addition_water_heater_sequencing
f_01M12F6MBCKAA7VVGRAHWGXB62.content: A new tank or tankless water heater in scope adds one day to the start of rough plumbing, since the tank is set before rough-in stubs into it; merely extending an existing water heater's vent through a new roof does not trigger this and is handled as a vent-extension task in exterior finishes.

f_01M12F6MBCFZ19SKZCYRF3HAWR.subject: addition_hvac_default
f_01M12F6MBCFZ19SKZCYRF3HAWR.content: HVAC type defaults to mini-split (short line-set rough, no separate rough-in phase) when scope language is ambiguous; "ducted," "duct work," or "air handler" trigger the longer duct-extension path instead, and ambiguity is flagged as needs_info.

f_01M12F6MBCYAZDJ77RWJJSKD95.subject: addition_truss_default
f_01M12F6MBCYAZDJ77RWJJSKD95.content: Stick-frame is the TCR default for small additions; truss procurement is included only when scope explicitly specifies trusses, roof span exceeds ~24 feet, footprint exceeds ~800 sqft, or the PM confirms it.

f_01M12F6MBCFGCBZC2YW7BEF2YQ.subject: addition_slopedlot_belowgrade_package
f_01M12F6MBCFGCBZC2YW7BEF2YQ.content: Sloped-lot or walkout additions require a below-grade package between foundation and framing: waterproofing and drainage board on the below-grade wall, a foundation drain with filter fabric sloped to daylight, gravel backfill, and continuous flashing — a stretch flat-lot schedules routinely miss.

f_01M12F6MBCQX0BK3VF574ACX4P.subject: addition_nonstandard_window_lead_trap
f_01M12F6MBCQX0BK3VF574ACX4P.content: Non-standard window sizes (outside stock size classes) are a silent lead-time trap because the schedule may default to stock lead time (21 days) for what is actually a custom-lead-time unit — size must be verified before ordering.

f_01M12F6MBCFQN35NGGD6VPRVGS.subject: addition_lvl_value_engineering_risk
f_01M12F6MBCFQN35NGGD6VPRVGS.content: "LVL omitted, sized per IRC" language in structural documents is a named risk — value-engineered engineered lumber tends to come back as a change order after final engineering, and should be carried as a flagged risk rather than assumed resolved.

f_01M12F6MBCZGE6X8D0GTBMM6TV.subject: addition_storage_crawl_habitability
f_01M12F6MBCZGE6X8D0GTBMM6TV.content: Storage or crawl levels under roughly 5' of clear height are not treated as habitable space, do not trigger habitable-space code paths, and their access (e.g. exterior barn doors) rides in exterior finishes rather than interior finishes.
